title: Attaining the entropy limit for union-closed families: paper, interval verification and checks
description:
We prove that every finite union-closed family with a nonempty member has an element lying in at least a fraction C* = 0.38288525996679779... of its members, where C* = 1/2 - (1 - q*) ln(1 + q*)/(2 ln 2) and q* is the root in (0, 1) of (1 - q) ln(1 - q) + q ln(1 + q) = 0. C* is the exact limit of the entropy method in the form of Liu and Jiang (arXiv:2609.08291); the best constants proved before were 0.38288525 (Jiang) and 0.3828852549667978 (Costa and Sadhu, arXiv:2610.02295). The auxiliary function is chosen so that both inequalities of the method, and their gradients, vanish at (q*, q*); their Hessians are certified positive definite on a square around that point, and an interval covering handles the rest of the unit square. With Jiang's global coupling the bound is strict: C* + ln^2(2N-1)/(128 N^2 ln^2 N) for a family of N >= 2 members.

preprintUnionClosedLimit/ holds the paper as a PDF; paper/ holds the LaTeX source (REVTeX 4.2) with four 3D figures; dist/ holds the PDF, the LaTeX source zip and the arXiv tarball; MasterUnionClosedLimit_masterzipfinal2.zip holds every file of the repository. checks/python/ holds the proof programs: tangency.py (ball-arithmetic Hessian certificate, python-flint) and verify_exact.py (interval certificate, adapted from Appendix B of Jiang's paper); checks/c, checks/cpp and checks/julia hold cross-checks; lean/ checks the rational breakpoints in the Lean 4 kernel with no axioms. scripts/run_all.sh runs everything.
